evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep asks 'Do you have about fifteen minutes?' but never frames the 10–15 minute time-box + dependable quote promise or waits for explicit yes before pivoting to probing.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Susanna Marcum), destination (Arlington), origin zip (76063, Grand Prairie area), moving date (mid-October, ~19th). Approximate size asked late: '1200 square feet' stated by customer, but rep did not systematically elicit it in discovery phase.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after probing already began: 'Other than price, what are the other questions that I can answer for you while I'm pulling this up?' — placed mid-call rather than upfront.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Strong follow-up on the wrapping/padding concern: Rep asked clarifying questions, customer explained the blanket vs. shrink-wrap issue, and rep went back a second time with 'Did you have any other concerns that I can address right now?' and dug into the garage/square footage disconnect multiple times throughout.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Partial: Rep acknowledged the padding/blanket concern with 'all of our movers are professionally trained vetted... wrapping padding protecting completely before we move your furniture that is part of their professional training' and 'So I definitely hope that bring some kind of ease' — but did not explicitly summarize/reflect back the customer's stated concerns in a clear 'So what I'm hearing is X, Y, Z' format.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type: apartment + garage (stated). Floors: first floor (stated). Rooms: not systematically asked. Walking distance: 10 minutes drive, both ground level. Additional stops/storage: customer mentioned items in storage facility to be moved later. Special considerations: garage full, not standard apartment contents. Missing: room count, which is a standard logistics item.
evidence_quotes.walkthrough_offered: Yes, correctly offered mid-call: 'what we do in situation such as this, so if you and I were really running through this estimate like for real and I have the address as I have the square footage, the number one thing that I would do is set up a virtual walkthrough, so that I can get eyes on the place.' This is the correct routing for a 1200 sq ft apartment with a full garage — the rep recognized complexity and deferred to walkthrough rather than completing estimate on call.

top_strength: Chauntelle handled the customer's significant past-trauma concern (damaged furniture from previous mover) with empathy and thorough reassurance, then pivoted to a smart walkthrough offer when the complexity of garage inventory made an accurate phone estimate impossible.
coaching_note: Lead with the quid pro quo framing (time-box + dependable quote promise) before any probing, and ask 'their agenda' in the same breath — don't wait until after you've already started gathering details.
booking_note: Customer stated 'more than likely, I'll have to go with another company' and ended the call without scheduling. Sales rep invited callback for future estimate but no commitment was made.
